claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can initially exist in a high-temperature BCC state.
Persistence of the high-temperature BCC state is governed by kinetic suppression of a thermodynamically driven ordering transformation.
Al content promotes the proposed ordering transformation.
The alloy has an intrinsic chemical instability favoring transition to a more ordered or secondary phase at lower temperatures.
Rapid cooling inhibits the atomic diffusion needed for ordering and transformation.
A moderate isothermal anneal permits the proposed transformation.
The relevant structural mediator is short-range ordering produced by local redistribution of Al and interactions with other elements in the BCC lattice.
Annealing enables atomic diffusion and rearrangement of Al and related species.
The proposed rearrangement lowers the alloy's free energy through an ordering transformation.
Rapid quenching freezes in the high-temperature BCC structure.
Phase stability is primarily dictated by whether sufficient atomic mobility is available to initiate ordering.
The annealed sample will exhibit a measurable phase transformation relative to the rapidly quenched baseline.
XRD or TEM of the annealed sample will reveal new ordered-phase features or lattice-parameter shifts.
The quenched baseline will retain the untransformed high-temperature BCC signature.
The proposed comparison applies only when the annealing temperature activates diffusion while remaining below melting or full homogenization conditions.
Absence of any statistically significant anneal-induced difference in phase composition, lattice parameters, or ordering features would falsify the hypothesis.
